newsitem.title: USA: PGA GOLF-NORMAN BEATS HOCH FOR $1 MILLION IN ARIZONA.
newsitem.headline: PGA GOLF-NORMAN BEATS HOCH FOR $1 MILLION IN ARIZONA.

text.p: Greg Norman sank a $1 million, 15-foot birdie putt on the final hole to edge Scott Hoch 1 up and win the Andersen Consulting World Championship of golf on Sunday.
The world's top-ranked golfer had to battle hard to beat the tenacious Hoch, whose 18-footer for birdie at the final hole narrowly missed.
"I had my chance on the last hole but I didn't convert," Hoch said. "Greg had an opportunity and converted. That's what the great players do."
Japan's Sasaki beat Scotland's Sam Torrance 2 and 1 in the 18-hole match for third prize.
Norman, who was never behind in the 36-hole final round, nonetheless was a little fortunate to win after blowing a large lead.
He was 4 up after 15 holes of the first round, and went into lunch with a handy 3 up halfway lead.

However, after being distracted by a photographer during his swing on the first tee, Norman started the second round disastrously, losing the next three holes to allow Hoch to get back to all square through 21 holes.

They stayed level until Norman won the 30th hole with a par to go 1 up. Hoch won the 33rd hole with a par to draw all square again, and had a chance to take the outright lead at the 34th hole, only to miss a six-foot birdie. Both players parred the second-last hole, and went to the par-five last with everything on the line.
After driving into a bunker, Norman blasted out to the fairway before hitting a nice third shot, an eight-iron from 156 yards.
As for his winning putt, Norman said: "I told myself to hit it solid. I read the green perfectly. I knew when I hit it, I'd made it."
To get to the final of the 32-man event, the richest in golf, Norman beat Craig Parry, Steve Elkington and David Frost in July, before thrashing Hisayuki Sasaki 5 and 4 in Saturday's semi-final.
The two-time British Open champion will take the next two months off to fine-tune his recently-refined swing, before resuming at the PGA Tour's Doral Open in Miami on March 6.
